headline: Ratified approval of $975,000 purchase of airplane hangar for Greater Lawrence Technical School, 8-1.
summary: The City Council held a special meeting and heard public comments on police, schools, veterans services, and hiring practices. The Council ratified its January 6th vote authorizing the City to purchase an airplane hangar at Lawrence Municipal Airport for $975,000 on behalf of Greater Lawrence Technical School, with conditions including repurchase by GLTS within five months and an appraisal and Airport Commission approval.
decisions: Declared DOC # 003/26 an emergency, passed by unanimous voice vote.

Ratified the approval of DOC # 003/26, the purchase of an airplane hangar at Lawrence Municipal Airport for $975,000 on behalf of Greater Lawrence Technical School, passed 8-1 (Laplante voting no, Delrosario absent).

MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING 
OF THE LAWRENCE CITY COUNCIL 
Monday, January 12, 2026 
 
A SPECIAL MEETING of the Lawrence City Council was held on Monday, January 12, 
2026. The meeting was called to Order at approximately 6:40 p.m. by City Council President, 
Jeovanny Rodriguez. This public meeting of the Lawrence City Council was conducted in 
person at Lawrence City Hall, 200 Common Street and via remote participation. Members of the 
public who attended this meeting were allowed to make comments during the portion of the 
meeting designated for public comment.  
 
He then asked the City Clerk, Eileen Bernal to call the roll:  
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – Present 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – Present  
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – Present 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – Present 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – Absent 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Absent 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – Present 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – Present  
Present - 7. Quorum established.   
 
NOTE: The Roll was called for Councilor Celina Reyes at 7:00 p.m.  
 
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION:  
 
The City Council President stated that members of the Public who had signed in for Public 
Participation would be allotted two and a half minutes to speak. He noted that their comments 
should be addressed to the Council as a whole and not to any individual member. Those 
participating were:  
 
H. Maali, 53 Chester Street. Mr. Maali stated that the citizens support the Police Unions. He 
noted that under the impeccable leadership of Chief Aguiler, the Police Department was doing 
well. He also spoke in support of the DPW and the Inspectional Services Department and 
encouraged the city to hire more inspectors. He commended the Public Schools and the 
leadership of Superintendent Ralph Carrero. He praised the Lawrence Teachers and their Union. 
He thanked the Veterans and encouraged the city to hire two new employees in veteran services. 
He encouraged them to activate the council on aging, and to pay the long-term employees as 
much as the new hires. He also spoke in support of Fire Chief Delaney who is doing the best job. 
“Lawrence Always Strong, Always United.”  
 
Richard Russell, 34 Cross Street. Former City Councilor Richard Russell expressed concern 
about the hiring of parking lot attendants and the hiring of employees without proper postings.
Page # 2 
Old Business: 
DOC # 003/26 Authorization to Purchase of Airplane Hanger at Lawrence Municipal 
Airport – John Lavoie, Greater Lawrence Technical School, 
Superintendent of Schools  
The Council President noted that at the January 6th meeting the City Council had voted to allow 
discussion on this Document with the waiving of Rule # 6. However, the item was not declared 
to be an emergency and the Charter requires an item to be an emergency if it is going to have a 
final disposition on the night it is introduced. In that regard, the Council needed to ratify their 
vote from January 6th 2026.  
 
Councilor Infante made a Motion to Declare DOC # 003/26 as an Emergency. Her Motion was 
seconded by Councilor Levy. This Motion PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
 
At the request of the Council President, the City Clerk read the Motion as previously Approved 
into the record again. Specifically, a “Motion for the City of Lawrence to purchase a hangar at 
the Lawrence Municipal Airport for $975,000 on behalf of Greater Lawrence Technical School 
(GLTS), with the understanding that GLTS will repurchase the hangar from the City within five 
(5) months for $975,000, plus any additional costs incurred by the City during the holding 
period. With three (3) caveats. (1) That the Council President is authorized to serve as a 
representative of the Council as needed during any negation period; (2) That the purchase is 
contingent upon a successful appraisal at or above the stated purchase price of $975,000; and (3) 
that the purchase is contingent upon an affirmative vote of Approval by the Lawrence Airport 
Commission  
 
Councilor Laplante, after being granted the floor, again expressed his concern with the rush to 
get this done. He stated that the date of the Airport Commission meeting was a week later than 
what he believed the Airport Manager said at their last meeting, and he the other 3 communities 
still had to vote on this item.  
Hearing no further discussion on the Motion, the Council President asked the Clerk for a Roll 
Call vote on the item:  
 
Councilor Marc Laplante [District F] – NO 
Councilor Gregory Delrosario [District C] – Absent 
Councilor Celina Reyes [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Councilor Stephany Infante [District E] – YES 
Councilor Vivian Marmol [District D] – YES 
Councilor Franklin Miguel [District A] – YES 
Councilor Rosaly Gonzalez [District B] – YES 
Council Vice President, Ana Levy [Councilor at Large] – YES 
Council President, Jeovanny Rodriguez [Councilor at Large] – YES 
 
DOC # 003/26 MOTION TO RATIFY the APPROVAL   PASSED
Page # 3 
As there was no other business before the Council, Councilor Infante made a Motion to Adjourn. 
Her Motion was seconded by Councilor Reyes. There was no discussion on the Motion and it 
PASSED by a Unanimous V oice V ote.  
The Meeting Adjourned at 7:06 p.m.
